newsitem.title: HONG KONG: KPI set to invest in China chain stores.
newsitem.headline: KPI set to invest in China chain stores.

text.p: Chemical fertiliser and agricultural products trader KPI Co Ltd said on Thursday it would jointly invest in supermarket and hypermarket chain store businesses in China with The China Retail Fund LDC (CRF).
KPI said it had signed a letter of intent with CRF to set up a joint venture company which would invest in the chain stores in major cities including Guangzhou, Shanghai and Beijing.
The venture, to be 51 percent owned by KPI and 49 percent by CRF, will involve initial working capital of HK$200 million, it said in a statement.

"Discussions are in progress with major PRC (People's Republic of China) supermarket operators and municipal officials as to the best way of developing and participating in the local super and hypermarket operations," it said.
CRF is a closed-end fund sponsored by American International Group with an objective of investing in retail and related distribution business in China.
CRF has total assets of US$165.7 million and its co-investment partners are companies controlled by China's Ministry of Internal Trade which administers wholesale and retail commercial activities.
